Asset: WELL-0075 (SW-24 Well 075, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Jan 2023 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 26 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0075-0012 on 2023-01-05 Report written: 08 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0075-0012 at 14:15 on 2023-01-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.6% of the pad area, estimated 1.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 400 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 320 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0075-0148 showed the wellhead at 42.3 °C with the air at 37.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0075-032

Asset: WELL-0075 (SW-24 Well 075, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 22 May 2026 08:00 · Finished: 22 May 2026 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 11 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0075-0186 on 2026-05-21 Report written: 24 May 2026

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0075-0186 at 11:30 on 2026-05-21 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.8% of the pad area, estimated 3.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 400 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 320 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.8 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0075-032 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.36% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
